ctx.x: So I got back on the job. I say hah, Ben, I say you do that shit to Charlie, I say you'll do it to me too. I say and if you do, man, I'll take a killing, but I ain't going to take no whipping. I say as large as you are, you know. There's no way. He mumbled something, you know. Gazed off into space, like he hasn't even heard me, you know. Well, I was ready for him. Never carried a knife, but I pulled my own coat. I say I'm getting so wild with this fighting, I . I won more fights on 52nd street than Sugar Ray did…

And they sent the northern soldiers south telling them broke their morale not to speak to the Negros you know and this This put everybody in a fighting mood. So one night, it's like D-Day. Kelley's Stables was on 52nd street between Seventh and Eighth and across the street was the Hickory House. Joseph Marsala

Mary McPartland, and Mary Osborne, they were over there a lot you know. It was -- Red Nova worked over there and the next block with -- which was Sixth Avenue and they renamed it that The Avenue of the Stars, between Sixth and Fifth, but the clubs was mostly about midway to the block and then they ended and then the 21 Club was further up the street. And that entailed the Three Deuces, The Downbeat next door, Tony's was like a supper club, they had a gate under the staircase, I forget this woman's name, Bill…
